description: Discriminator: two commands are marshalled back to back (a 70000-byte value followed by a small one); after the first is unmarshalled, does the second decode to what was written? Prefix: the harness builds both commands and marshals them into one buffer with the implementation's own codec. Controls: the prerequisite prints the written keys and lengths and the total wire bytes, and the result prints the decoded first-value length, the second command's decoded fields, whether they match and how many bytes remain.

harness.description: In-package Go test that writes two commands into one stream and decodes them in order, reporting what the second one becomes.
semantic_changes: harness-only scaffolding: no replica is constructed; the test calls the state codec directly on a buffer holding two commands
two commands in one buffer model a batch or a recorder that appends commands, which is how the implementation writes them

legality.derivation: The wire form of a command sequence is exactly concatenated Command marshallings, which is what batches and the durable record append.
legality.applicability: One stream, two commands, no replica.
unresolved: the durable recorder's own append order is a separate observation

grounding.derivation: The event reports what the second command decoded to and how many bytes remain, which is the consequence of the truncated length.
grounding.applicability: The first command carried a value beyond the length field's range.

observable_properties.description: The command following an oversized value must still decode to what was written.

uncertainties: the check does not attach the shifted stream to a replica reader, so the reader's own reaction is unobserved
the shipped configuration's 1000-byte commands never reach the boundary
